request.description: A single complete slender architectural masonry pilaster for a whimsical pixel-art dungeon sidescroller, FRONT elevation orthographic, strictly flat side-on 2D. On this 64x96 transparent canvas draw one pillar centered, only 24 pixels wide and about 80 pixels tall: a small plain stepped 24-wide capital at top, a straight 18-wide shaft of four large rectangular stone courses with recessed horizontal mortar and broad quiet planes, and a modest stepped 24-wide foot block. Cool muted violet stone matching a dark indigo dungeon wall. Simple controlled top-left lighting, narrow pale-violet top edge, medium-violet front, dark right side and deep recessed mortar. Sparse tiny chips only. Crisp native pixels and connected chunky shading. Keep the entire silhouette with generous transparent clearance. This is functional support stone, not a decorative hero prop: no gold, red/orange, flames, carvings, gems, skulls, cracks, plants, objects, floor or background. Style reference supplies economical clean clusters and contour discipline only, not the skeleton subject or its palette.

style_image.usage_description: Rattlebones is Dungeon Matcher's approved primary rendering reference. Match native crisp contours, economical broad connected planes and restrained top-left shading only. Draw architecture; do not copy his body, face, costume or palette.

quote.grid_recovery: Creation recovers the pixel grid the model drew with Unzoom. An exact grid is kept; drift of at most one pixel is recovered on the expected grid. Images with a background must fill the canvas, so any other size is redrawn with image-to-pixel-art on the generated box only. Sprites without a background keep their own pixels, centred on the canvas, while the drawn pixel is close to the requested one; coarser or oversized sprites are redrawn. Experimental 16x16 creation always uses image-to-pixel-art. Editing and inpainting start at 32x32 and never use image-to-pixel-art conversion.
